sizeMatchedRandomReference.statistic: Mean answer-gist cosine in127uniformly sampled distinct-upload candidate pairs; count-matched descriptive baseline, not a calibrated null.

commonSupportStandardization.weightDefinition: Within the bins containing both quarantine strata, weight each bin by its pooled neighbor-pair count, then apply the identical weights to the separate group means.
limitations: Quarantine is constructed from question similarity; unsupported high-similarity bins cannot identify a cross-quarantine comparison.
The retained common-support pool differs from all127neighbors. Standardization does not replace the original all-neighbor/cross-group descriptive summaries.
Coarse bins leave within-bin question-similarity, length, topic and source selection differences. No causal session-reuse or answer-agreement claim follows.
Neighbor pairs share candidates/uploads; no independent-pair confidence interval or inferential p-value is reported.

benchmarkGuard.rule: Link uploads if any exactly normalized question repeats, any question cosine>=0.80, OR at least three cross-upload question pairs cosine>=0.40. Connected components are conservative quarantine groups, not proven original-session families.

representationNuisance.partialRankDefinition: Pearson correlation of title and caption rank residuals after separate OLS projection on intercept and ranked nuisance variables. No p-value or independent-pair uncertainty interval.

titleCosine.method: OLS projection on intercept, absolute log duration ratio, mean log duration in minutes, and absolute log caption word-count ratio; within-minus-between means of residual cosine. Descriptive conditioning, not a causal or speaker effect.

captionCosine.method: OLS projection on intercept, absolute log duration ratio, mean log duration in minutes, and absolute log caption word-count ratio; within-minus-between means of residual cosine. Descriptive conditioning, not a causal or speaker effect.

leaveOnePublisherOut.meaning: Deterministic influence range, not a confidence interval.

model.parameterScale: 0.5B family; bounded CPU baseline, not established state of the art

The exact recorded room temperature was 23°C (73°F).

interpretation: These are eight held-out AI-digest reconstruction questions and two deliberately unsupported controls, not a model quality ranking.
Train-only RAG intentionally excludes the target source group and answer; this is sparse-source transfer, not an ordinary answer-present RAG comparison.
Token F1 measures lexical overlap. Supplied-label membership does not establish entailment or factual correctness.
Control counts require the literal INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE marker. A spaced refusal such as Insufficient evidence. scores zero; this is formatting compliance, not general refusal accuracy.
The 40-new-token generation cap and 192-token training cap can affect lexical scores; length and citation-normalized sensitivities remain separate checks.
Observed split quarantine does not rule out pretrained-model contamination or unknown source-session overlap.
One LoRA closed control output invents an exact studio temperature (23°C); this is a concrete unsupported response, not inferred from lexical scores.
benchmarkAudit.adapterVerification: Portable archive/member hashes verified; adapter weight bytes match the original training receipt. Package README/config normalization is described by its separate manifest. No external model cache is required for this audit.

limitations: AI digest questions and answer gists are a one-practitioner paraphrase source, not literal turns or independently verified answers.
Pair scores share questions, uploads and publishers; numerical association is descriptive, not independent human evidence.
Question lexical components and quarantine links do not establish semantic equivalence or repeated original sessions.
The count-matched random reference does not match publisher, format or word-length distributions and is not a calibrated null.
Partial ranks and residual cosine condition on observed length variables only; they do not establish causal mediation or isolate speaker identity.
Frozen caption/title vectors use the historical masked MiniLM representations; no new encoder was executed.

limits: The broader refusal pattern was defined after output inspection and is not human refusal or correctness annotation.
The positive-control source answers are intentionally supplied from training; their overlap/citation scores are not held-out generalization.
The twelve text-label examples are balanced on a dictionary heuristic; method concordance is not accuracy or corpus prevalence.
All nine parsed themes collapse to contact_forecast; do not use this failed probe as empirical theme distribution.
No exact answer evidence spans passed the specified source-substring rule.
Citation-stripped overlap preserves the original scores as separate metrics; no model parameters are optimized on this diagnostic.
Generation cap hits document censoring; no longer-budget generation experiment was executed.

optionOrder.interpretation: Observed prompt sensitivity; no reversed valid output selects the new first option, so a simple deterministic first-option-copy account does not fit this probe. No annotation accuracy is established.

currentFamily.interpretation: Same-item schema and quotation-compliance comparison across different architectures/tokenizers/runtimes; not semantic-label accuracy, parameter-scale causality, held-out QA improvement or general model ranking.

limits: Original outputs, original dictionary labels and the five-arm held-out pilot remain preserved.
Paired option changes use only items parsed under both prompts; all parse failures remain visible.
The stricter conditional pattern is a post-hoc lexical sensitivity, not a corrected human reference.
All models can collapse to one conditional label; dictionary concordance is not annotation accuracy.
The current-family model receives text only. No image, video, speech, GPU or current-family fine-tuning experiment is implied.
A shared96-token cap is not an identical word/context budget across tokenizers.
